question_text: In △ABC, if cot(A/2), cot(B/2), cot(C/2) are in A.P., prove that a, b, c are in A.P.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write each cotangent over Δ
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. cot(A/2) = s(s−a)/Δ: the bracket carries the SAME letter as the angle, which is the opposite of tan(A/2).
steps.memory_tip: cot(A/2) = s(s−a)/Δ — the bracket carries the same letter as the angle. tan(A/2) uses the other two.

recall.must_convey: That cot(A/2) = s(s−a)/Δ, and the same pattern gives cot(B/2) and cot(C/2).
accept: cot half A is s into s minus a over delta
multiply top and bottom so the denominator becomes Heron's product
the bracket carries the same letter as the angle
cot half A ante s into s minus a by delta
write all three cotangents over delta

steps.why: An arithmetic progression is a statement about differences, and differences are easy only when the three terms share a factor. Written over Δ, all three carry the same s/Δ.

steps.label: Use the A.P. condition
steps.margin_note: The other mark. Dividing by s/Δ is allowed because s and Δ are both positive; then the 2s cancels from both sides.
steps.memory_tip: Three terms are in A.P. when twice the middle equals the sum of the outer two: 2cot(B/2) = cot(A/2) + cot(C/2).

lines.text: (in an A.P. x, y, z, the middle term gives 2y = x + z)
(take 2s from both sides and multiply by −1)
∴ a, b, c are in A.P.

recall.must_convey: That 2cot(B/2) = cot(A/2) + cot(C/2) reduces to 2(s−b) = (s−a) + (s−c), giving 2b = a + c.
accept: twice the middle term equals the sum of the other two
the common factor s over delta cancels
two s minus two b equals two s minus a plus c so two b is a plus c
madhya term ki rendu rettu ante migatha rendintiki sum
cancel s over delta and the two s to get two b equals a plus c
heard_as: two b equals a plus c

steps.why: Three numbers are in A.P. when twice the middle one equals the sum of the outer two. The common factor s/Δ divides out, and the 2s on both sides cancels, leaving only 2b = a + c.
common_mistakes: Writing cot(A/2) + cot(B/2) = 2cot(C/2), which uses the wrong middle term.
Cancelling the 2s wrongly and finishing with b = a + c.
